title: Breaking Big Problems Into Small Ones

beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you again.
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, we worked backwards. Mina had nine stickers after losing three. So we added the three back, and found she started with twelve.
beats.caption: Last time: work backwards · 9 + 3 = 12

beats.vo: Today is chapter four of Problem Solver. It's called, Breaking Big Problems Into Small Ones.
beats.caption: Chapter 4 · Breaking Big Problems Into Small Ones

beats.vo: Have you ever looked at a job and thought, whoa, that's way too big? Hmm. Today, I'll show you a trick that makes big jobs feel small.
beats.caption: Ever felt a job was way too big?

beats.vo: Meet Riya. It's Sunday morning, and Mum calls out, Riya, Nani is coming this evening. Please clean your room!
beats.caption: "Riya, please clean your room!"

beats.vo: Riya looks around. Toys on the floor. Books everywhere. And the bed is one big, crumpled mess. Oh no!
beats.caption: Toys, books, a messy bed… Oh no!

beats.vo: Riya just stands there. Where do I even start? It all feels too big. What would you do, if you were Riya? Think for a moment.
beats.caption: Where do I even start? What would you do?

beats.vo: Here's a smart idea. Don't clean the whole room at once. Split it into small jobs. Pick up the toys. Put the books on the shelf. Make the bed.
beats.caption: Toys · Books · Bed: three small jobs

beats.vo: Now Riya does one small job at a time. Toys, done. Books, done. Bed, done. And look! The whole room is clean, and it didn't even feel hard.
beats.caption: One small job at a time → clean room!

beats.vo: What Riya did has a special name. It's called decomposition.
beats.caption: That trick is called DECOMPOSITION

beats.vo: De, com, po, si, tion. A long word, but the meaning is simple. Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller, easier parts.
beats.caption: Breaking a big problem into small parts

beats.vo: Think about eating a roti. You can't stuff the whole roti in your mouth at once! You tear it into small pieces, and eat one bite at a time. Yum.
beats.caption: A roti: one small bite at a time

beats.vo: Each piece is a small task. A small task is one simple job that you can finish on its own.
beats.caption: Small task = one job you can finish

beats.vo: That night, Riya has another big job. Packing her school bag for Monday.
beats.caption: Big job: pack the school bag

beats.vo: What small jobs are hiding inside it? Her books, her water bottle, her lunch box, and her pencil box.
beats.caption: Books · Bottle · Lunch box · Pencil box

beats.vo: Now let's put them in order. One, check today's timetable. Two, put in those books. Three, fill the water bottle. Four, add the lunch box.
beats.caption: Timetable → Books → Bottle → Lunch box

beats.vo: Why check the timetable first? Because it tells you which books you need! So after you break a job, you also decide the order. What comes first, next, and last.
beats.caption: Then decide: first, next, last

beats.vo: Let's go back to the evening. Nani arrives, and it's so hot! Riya decides to make her some nimbu pani.
beats.caption: Nani is here! Riya makes nimbu pani

beats.vo: First, squeeze the lemons. Then, add water. Next, stir in some sugar. And last, pour it into a glass, and serve.
beats.caption: Squeeze → Water → Sugar → Pour & serve

beats.vo: Could Riya pour and serve it first? No way! There's nothing to pour yet. Serving comes last, because you can only serve it after it's made.
beats.caption: Serve first? Nothing to pour! Serve LAST

beats.vo: Nani loves maths puzzles. She asks Riya, what is twenty three plus forty five?
beats.caption: Nani's puzzle: what is 23 + 45?

beats.vo: Riya breaks each number into tens and ones. Twenty three is twenty and three. Forty five is forty and five.
Add the tens. Twenty plus forty equals sixty. Now add the ones. Three plus five equals eight.
beats.caption: Tens: 20 + 40 = 60 · Ones: 3 + 5 = 8

beats.vo: Put them together. Sixty and eight make sixty eight! Two small sums were easier than one big one.
Nani smiles, and asks a trickier one. What is six times fourteen? Hmm. That's a big one to do in your head.
beats.caption: What is 6 × 14?

beats.vo: So let's break fourteen into ten and four. Look at the dots. Six rows of ten, and six rows of four.
beats.caption: Break it up: 14 = 10 + 4

beats.vo: Six times ten is sixty. And six times four is twenty four.
Now add them up. Sixty plus twenty four equals eighty four. So, six times fourteen is eighty four!
beats.caption: 60 + 24 = 84. So 6 × 14 = 84!

beats.vo: Riya's cousin Arjun is a coder. He makes games! And guess what? He uses decomposition every single day.
beats.caption: Coders use decomposition every day!

beats.vo: Arjun wants to make a cricket game. That's huge! So he breaks it into parts. Draw the pitch. Make the bat swing. Move the ball. Keep the score.
beats.caption: Pitch · Bat · Ball · Score

beats.vo: Each part gets its own step by step plan. And a step by step plan to solve a problem is called an algorithm. Big programs are built from small, clear parts, in the right order.
beats.caption: Algorithms are built in small parts too

beats.vo: Game time! Remember Riya's room? Which of these is NOT a small part of cleaning a room? Pick up toys. Make the bed. Fly a kite. Put books on the shelf. Think!
beats.caption: Which is NOT part of cleaning a room?

beats.vo: Fly a kite! It's lots of fun, but it doesn't help clean the room at all. Every small part should help finish the big job.
beats.caption: Fly a kite doesn't help clean the room!

beats.vo: One more! Riya's class is having a party. Here are the steps, all mixed up. Buy snacks. Set up, and enjoy. Pick a date. Make a guest list. What's the best order? Pause, and think.
beats.caption: Party steps are mixed up! What's the order?

beats.vo: First, pick a date. Then, make a guest list, so you know who's coming. Next, buy snacks. And last, set up, and enjoy! Plan first, then shop, then party.
beats.caption: Date → Guest list → Snacks → Set up & enjoy

beats.vo: Okay champ, your turn. Here's a practice check, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: Tomorrow is Nani's birthday, and Riya wants to make her a card. Break, make a birthday card, into four small steps, in order. Pause the video, and try it on paper.
beats.caption: Break 'make a birthday card' into 4 steps

beats.vo: Here's one way. One, fold the paper. Two, draw a picture on the front. Three, write a message inside. Four, sign your name, and give it. Folding comes first, because you need a card before you can draw on it! Brilliant!
beats.caption: Fold → Draw → Write → Sign & give

beats.vo: Let's remember what we learned. Decomposition means breaking a big job into small jobs.
beats.caption: Big job → small jobs

beats.vo: Then, put the small jobs in order.
beats.caption: Put the small jobs in order

beats.vo: Do one small job at a time, just like eating a roti, bite by bite.
beats.caption: Do one small job at a time

beats.vo: And algorithms, and even big sums, are built in parts too.
beats.caption: Algorithms & sums are built in parts

beats.vo: Chapter four, done! You can break big jobs into small steps, just like Riya. Super work, champ!
beats.caption: Chapter 4 done!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
